nodes.name: Every 2 Hours
nodes.notes: Two hours, not fifteen minutes. The cart window below is measured in hours, so a tighter schedule would add API load without finding anything new.

nodes.name: WooCommerce: Open Orders
nodes.notes: An empty WooCommerce list is a normal answer, not an error - and a node that emits zero items silently ends the branch (alwaysOutputData does not help: n8n only applies it when the node has no outputs at all, and this one has an error output). Full Response guarantees exactly one item, so "no orders" is a state the workflow can see and act on.

parameters.query:
INSERT INTO cart_nudges (order_id, email, cart_value, currency, hours_abandoned, execution_id)
VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5, $6)
ON CONFLICT (order_id) DO NOTHING
RETURNING id, order_id;

nodes.name: Claim Nudge
nodes.notes: One nudge per cart, ever. The row is claimed before the email is sent, not after - a crash between the two costs one missed email, which is far cheaper than a second one.

nodes.name: Converted Since
nodes.notes: The customer paid between the list query and now. No email.

nodes.name: Nudge Copy
nodes.notes: Both outputs of the LLM call land here. One node, one output shape, so a model outage changes the copy and nothing else.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ template: 'abandoned_cart', to: $json.email, subject: $json.subject, body: $json.body, idempotency_key: 'cart-' + $json.order_id, variables: { pay_url: $json.payment_url, order_number: $json.order_number } }) }}

parameters.query:
UPDATE cart_nudges
SET sent_at = now(), delivered = $2, subject = $3, copy_source = $4,
    copy_error = $5, detail = $6
WHERE order_id = $1
RETURNING id, delivered;

nodes.name: Record Nudge Outcome
nodes.notes: The claim row is updated, not inserted again. delivered = false is what you filter on when a client asks which nudges silently failed.

nodes.name: WooCommerce: Product Stock
nodes.notes: Full Response, so an empty product list is one visible item rather than a branch that quietly stops.

parameters.query:
INSERT INTO restock_tasks
  (task_key, product_id, sku, product_name, stock_quantity, threshold,
   out_of_stock, execution_id)
VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5, $6, $7, $8)
ON CONFLICT (task_key) DO NOTHING
RETURNING id, task_key;

nodes.name: Alert Supplier Channel
nodes.notes: Terminal on purpose: this node has no error output. After three tries a Slack outage fails the execution, and the failure is picked up by workflow 04. An error output here would swallow it.
